expected_wrong_value: C: central diamond aperture incorrectly declared impossible
mechanism: Red/blue split the two discarded axis-aligned corner legs and map them to E square-hole sides. Predict accepting E as the central-corner result by mistaking discarded pre-cut boundary traces for surviving cut edges, and rejecting C (the competing central diamond) as impossible. The actual diagonal cut remains black and proves that this role transfer is false. This is not simply matching the true cut to C and reversing can/cannot.

mathematical_proof.method: Independent exact fold-orbit enumeration, source JPG and formal PNG viewed at native scale
mathematical_proof.coordinate_setup: Original square [-1,1]^2; perpendicular half folds leave Q=[0,1]^2, up to orientation. Every removal unfolds by (u,v)->(s*u,t*v) for s,t in {-1,+1}. A straight corner clip meets both adjacent sides at positive distances a,b. Its cut segment has two nonzero components.

exhaustive_four_cases.unfolded_removal: Four separate right triangles at all four original outer corners
exhaustive_four_cases.construction: Remove (1-u)/a+(1-v)/b<1 near (1,1), with 0<a,b<1; reflect across both axes. The outer boundary is an octagon.

exhaustive_four_cases.unfolded_removal: Two V notches at opposite top and bottom side midpoints
exhaustive_four_cases.construction: Remove u/a+(1-v)/b<1 near (0,1); reflection in u=0 joins two half triangles into one V notch; reflection in v=0 creates its opposite.

exhaustive_four_cases.unfolded_removal: Two V notches at opposite left and right side midpoints
exhaustive_four_cases.construction: Remove (1-u)/a+v/b<1 near (1,0); reflect in v=0, then u=0.

exhaustive_four_cases.unfolded_removal: One central diamond or axis-diagonal rhombus hole
exhaustive_four_cases.construction: Remove u/a+v/b<1 near (0,0); unfolded hole |x|/a+|y|/b<1. For a=b its vertices are (+/-a,0),(0,+/-a).

mathematical_proof.exclusion_of_E: Only the centre-centre corner can make a bounded internal hole. That hole has four oblique sides with directions (+/-a,+/-b); no side is parallel to an original sheet edge when a,b>0. E has four axis-parallel inner sides, so is not that hole. The other three cases meet the outer boundary, and cannot make E either. All A/B/C/D have explicit constructions above. Thus E is uniquely impossible.
mathematical_proof.freedom_preserved: The final displayed clipped corner is an illustrative possible corner, not an additional restriction to one fold-corner type. All four corners were enumerated; no annotation may choose one as a new given.
mathematical_proof.candidate_color_semantics: Source color is confined to two dashed legs lying strictly in the removed corner except their cut endpoints. They outline absent/discarded material, not the surviving sheet. The actual diagonal cut and all surviving material boundaries remain black. Even a physical-color reading of those discarded edges leaves no finite colored surviving edge to transport. E alone receives new color, and E is already geometrically impossible; other samples, including the unique correct one, remain unmodified. No source fold/cut count, crease style, fill, or option geometry changes.

reference_and_history.current_reference: Current Solid167 C01: two existing source features and two candidate boundary groups are compared with red and blue; no old D color mapping is inherited.
reference_and_history.migration: There is only one true source cut. Rather than inventing two cuts, this design distinguishes the two actual discarded corner traces and compares their directions/roles with existing E aperture or notch edges.
reference_and_history.earlier_r01: r01 uses operation indicators (fold-axis guides for Plane194, motion arrows for Plane245). r02 uses only the two dashed legs of the removed corner. Therefore source geometry-role evidence changes, not just style. R01 pixels and all its output remain immutable.
reference_and_history.old_Plane245_attempt: The old A design compared the actual diagonal cut and one vertical ghost leg with the A central square. This design does not color the actual cut, uses both ghost legs, and compares them with E exterior corner notches while retaining its true central diamond. That is a different receiving geometry and a double-counting hypothesis, not old input relabeling.
reference_and_history.old_Plane194_prescreen: A prior untested prescreen warned that coloring ghost legs could be read as changing the cut. Here source true cut remains solid black, both ghosts remain dashed outside retained material, all four cut-corner constructions remain allowed, and no line is added. The proposed error is explicitly accepting the wrong E inner boundary by discarded-versus-surviving edge confusion.
